The thought passes without answer. You return to the book.

The committee chapter is drier than the opening, but more useful. Conclave students do not vote in Council sessions; they prepare briefs, observe negotiations, serve on Academy commissions, and learn which minor procedural decisions can quietly change a larger dispute. A vacant seat can leave work delayed for years without anyone admitting that delay is the point.

A penciled note beside one example reads: *Ask who chose the committee.*

The library remains companionably quiet. Caelindra turns a page at the window table, makes a small dissatisfied sound at something in her protocol text, then continues reading. Professor Stone’s blue pencil travels steadily down his ledger beneath the spiral stair.

By the time the lamps need trimming, you have a clearer sense of the Council’s machinery—and how much of it seems designed to conceal where responsibility begins.
